Linux Sysadmin for +10yrs which language should I start to learn?
I'd say C, so you can understand and fix your tools.
Java if you want to find a job fast and have flexibility. C++ if you want to work with high-end stuff. Can never go wrong with node.js tho.
Python is always a good option, Go seems to be a up-and-comer though with lots of potential. I'd say stick with either of those and you should be good.

If you were a sysadmin of a web app then you should understand the architecture of web applications. Personally, I end up having to touch the database (more than I should) and messing with the front end code.

I'd advise you to go down a strange route. You understand how to set up environments. Learn docker (they're like micro vm's). Setup a docker for a mysql (really easy to learn, like stupid easy, hard to master) and a docker with an apache php server. Learn the basics of php, (simple starting point) and when you have completed something a bit better more complex than a hello world I'd start moving into making a python web server. Also, during all of this pick up backbone.js and play with it.

You would end up being a full stack guy, not just in the DevOps world.
